subject: Post-call: connection pooling & parallelism pilot — proposed quotas and next steps
messages:
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Tom Benson <tbenson@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 15:08:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: connection pooling & parallelism pilot — proposed quotas and next steps

Tom — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a clean path into a short pilot: 

Recap / requirements we heard from Acme Health: 
- Latency target: p95 end-to-end generation < 150–200 ms for ~512-token sequences for synchronous (non-streaming) calls; for streaming (SSE/HTTP2) p95 acceptable up to ~250 ms for first-byte but steady chunk latency needs to be <100 ms.
- Throughput: baseline of ~20 concurrent users during business hours leading to a steady-state of ~120 parallel requests (peak bursts to ~180 for short windows).
- Streaming: partial output should be flushed as tokens are produced; chunk sizes ~32–64 tokens preferred.
- Connection pooling: client expects long-lived sockets (~keep-alive) and reuse across requests; prefer per-API-key pool scoping.

Proposed pilot (what Redwood can offer quickly):
1) Reserved concurrency: commit to a pilot allocation of 100 parallel request slots in us-west region with burst allowance up to 150 for 30s windows while we tune batching.
2) Connection pool baseline: default shared pool = 32 sockets per API key; Dedicated pilot option: increase to 64 persistent sockets per API key.
3) Streaming support: we will enable chunked streaming with 32-token flushes and provide a sample client impl we used in the demo.
4) Observability: we’ll add your telemetry collection (endpoint-level p50/p95/p99, connection reuse, token counts) to the pilot dashboard; KPI cadence weekly.
5) Pilot length & success criteria: 6-week pilot; success = sustained p95 <200 ms for sync and initial-byte <250 ms for streaming with <10% error overhead and average connection reuse > 10 requests/socket.

Attached: pilot metrics template and mutual action plan (map-acme-pilot-milestones.docx, acme-pilot-metrics.xlsx).

Next steps (suggested):
- You confirm the pilot targets and the primary integration contact (ops@acmehealth.com OK?)
- We provision a pilot key and walk through a short integration checklist (tokenization, max payloads, backpressure behavior)
- Kickoff call to align security checklist & scope on Fri 10/22 if that works for you.

If that looks right I’ll send a short pilot agreement + price delta for the reserved concurrency vs hosted baseline.

Thanks — Mateo

--
Mateo Alvarez
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Post-call: connection pooling & parallelism pilot — proposed quotas and next steps

Thanks Mateo — helpful summary. A couple of clarifying Qs before we lock the pilot: 

1) For streaming: can Redwood guarantee initial-byte p95 <250 ms under the proposed reserved concurrency and burst assumptions? We have real-time UX SLAs that make this a hard requirement.
2) Is the connection pool scoping per-API-key or per-account? We have multiple services that will each use their own key, and we need predictable per-service sockets.
3) How does tokenization overhead affect latency targets? Our inputs include medical notes with lots of punctuation and occasional long fields.

Also pls confirm whether the burst windows (150 for 30s) are enforced soft-burst vs hard-throttle and if there are credits applied.

Tom

Subject: Re: Post-call: connection pooling & parallelism pilot — proposed quotas and next steps

Tom — great questions. Answers inline below and some options so we can finalize the pilot agreement quickly.

1) Streaming initial-byte p95 guarantee:
- Under the reserved concurrency allocation (100) with a 150 burst, we can commit to an *initial-byte p95 < 250 ms* for the pilot provided the client uses our recommended streaming client (keeps socket warm, payload chunking >= 32 tokens) and we instrument your integration so we can observe tokenization variance. This will be included as a pilot SLO.
- Note: sustained bursts beyond configured windows will trigger throttling behavior. We can model a soft-burst policy that uses token credits for short overages (exhausted credits => 429).

2) Connection pool scoping:
- By default our hosted plan scopes pools per-API-key (recommended). That maps cleanly to your per-service requirements. For Dedicated / reserved pilots we can scope pools per-API-key and increase the socket limit (32 -> 64).

3) Tokenization overhead & latency:
- Tokenization typically adds ~5–15 ms depending on payload shape; pathological long fields can add more. We’ll share a small harness so you can run sample inputs through our tokenizer in your environment and we’ll include the measured tokenization time in the dashboard.

Burst semantics & credits:
- Proposal: soft burst window (30s) up to +50% of committed concurrency with a small credit bucket (500 credit sec) to smooth spikes. If you exceed credits we 429 and optionally redirect to lower-cost fallback model variants.

Commercial framing for the pilot:
- Pilot reserved concurrency: 100 committed slots; burst to 150 with credits.
- Pricing: pilot discount applied; estimate attached (redwood-dedicated-pricing-v1.pdf).
- Security: we’ll run a scoped security intake (SOC2 artifacts, KMS integration checklist) during week 1.

If you’re comfortable with that framing I’ll: 
- Draft the short pilot MSA + SLO exhibit
- Provision a pilot API key and send sample client snippets for streaming/backpressure
- Schedule kickoff Fri 10/22 with security included

Would you like us to make the connection pool per-service the default for the pilot (I recommend yes)?

— Mateo
